about: Timmy Turner's dad from The Fairly OddParents glares sideways with his teeth bared and his eyes narrowed, mid-snarl, the face he makes right before hissing his neighbour's name: "Dinkleberg..." Dad blames Dinkleberg for every misfortune, no matter how unrelated, and the meme borrows that reflex. People use it to pin a problem on their favourite scapegoat or to parody someone who blames the same culprit for everything.
origin: The Fairly OddParents aired on Nickelodeon starting in 2001. Dad's grudge against his friendly neighbour Dinkleberg was a running gag, and the snarling still became a reaction image in the late 2000s.
usage:
There is only one box, at the top. Write the question or problem there, like "who broke the build?" or "why is the Wi-Fi slow?". The image itself supplies the answer: everyone who knows the meme hears Dad muttering "Dinkleberg...". You can also spell it out with a second line in the same box if your audience may not get it.

It works when the blame is obviously unfair or reflexive: blaming the intern, blaming the new patch, blaming the ref, blaming Mercury retrograde.
ideas: who ate my leftovers from the office fridge?
why did the deploy fail at 5pm on a Friday?
who keeps leaving the cereal box empty?
why did my team lose the match?
why is my grade lower than I expected?
